The overall goal of the project is to contribute to the efforts of ensuring that citizens of Isiolo and Marsabit counties benefit from inclusive and participatory county governance development processes.

The projects interventions will be focused on the North Frontier counties of Isiolo and Marsabit. Despite the goodwill of the Constitution to reduce the levels of marginalisation across Kenya, the residents of Isiolo and Marsabit counties still live on the periphery of society, systemically excluded from the mainstream social, political, economic, and cultural development. They experience recurrent challenges of abject poverty, condensed economic activities limited to pastoralism, political under-representation, and limited inclusion and public participation in the counties development agenda. Both counties are Arid and Semi-Arid Land (ASAL) and are negatively affected by climate change, which is often a trigger of conflict. The latter occurs specifically among pastoralists communities belonging to different ethnic groups, who, because of extreme climatic events, are forced to look for pasture and other natural resources, often invading the boundaries of other communities and counties.
The geographical inaccessibility of many areas of especially Marsabit County but lso border areas of Isiolo county also exacerbates the marginalisation of its communities, with the majority of the State institutions unable and unwilling to penetrate these areas. Building on the 2030 Agenda for sustainable development and the principle of leaving no one behind, the project will focus its interventions in these two counties.
It is expected that at the end of the intervention, the project will contribute to the efforts of ensuring that citizens of Isiolo and Marsabit counties benefit from inclusive and participatory county governance development processes and that the county Governments of Isiolo and Marsabit, will increasingly drive transparency, and accountability actions, including on climate change and Natural resource management. In addition, the residents will be exposed to contextualised multi-door approaches to justice, including court annexed mediation (CAM) and Alternative justice systems (AJS) platforms, which will increase their chances of effectively solving their disputes in a fairer, cheaper, and more effective manner. It is also envisaged that there will be improved ability of women, especially young women, in Isiolo and Marsabit counties to access public information and effectively participate in county-level governance processes as well as an improved capacity of the county Governments of Isiolo and Marsabit to implement gender-responsive county-level climate change and NRM Actions for inclusive climate resilience development.

description.narrative: Immediate Outcome 1: Improved Ability of Justice Seekers and Providers to Use Inclusive MultiDoor Approaches to Justice in Isiolo and Marsabit Counties Through the project, IDLO strengthened inclusive, multidoor approaches to justice in Isiolo and Marsabit by supporting the replication of CAM (Court Annexed Mediation)stations, the establishment of AJS (Alternative Justice Systems) Suites, the development of operational frameworks, and capacity development for judicial officers, mediators and AJS actors. While some output targets were not fully achieved, all outcome targets were exceeded, contributing to stronger access to both formal and communitybased justice mechanisms. IDLO supported National Steering Committee on the Implementation of the Alternative Justice Systems Policy (NaSCIAJS) to operationalize AJS through the development of key frameworks, including the Code of Conduct for AJS practitioners, Case Registration Form, Guidelines on the Use of AJS Suites, and County Action Plans for Isiolo and Marsabit. AJS Suites were launched in Isiolo and Marsabit in 2024 with support for essential infrastructure. According to the 2024/2025 State of the Judiciary and the Administration of Justice Report (SOJAR), six County Action Plans were launched during the reporting period, two of which were supported by IDLO, bringing the national total to 13. AJS use also increased: 677 cases were concluded in counties where the Judiciary actively monitored referrals, including Isiolo and Marsabit. In Isiolo, the AJS Suite handled 139 cases in its first year, resolving 134, a 96.4% resolution rate. IDLO also supported the launch of the AJS Prison Model at Isiolo Prison in September 2024. The model applies restorative justice to minor offences, supporting reconciliation, rehabilitation and prison decongestion. Initial implementation resulted in 60 cases resolved and 37 detainees conditionally released. The model has since informed wider Judiciary efforts, including periodic sentence reviews for petty offenders. Under CAM, IDLO supported the establishment of fully operational CAM registries at Isiolo and Marsabit Law Courts, trained mediators and supported community sensitization. The two CAM stations handled 190 cases and resolved 133, helping reduce backlogs and providing faster, more affordable justice. Draft Justice seekers saved an estimated KES 26 million from the 133 resolved cases. Nationally, SOJAR 2024/2025 reported 14 new CAM registries, bringing the total number of CAM court stations to 94, including 14 supported by IDLO. CAM referrals also increased nationally from 6,573 to 9,843 cases, a 50% increase, with 8,828 cases concluded, representing a 90% resolution rate. IDLO further supported frameworks for private and family mediation, including guidelines that enabled 49 private mediation cases to be filed and concluded by the Judiciary. Immediate Outcome 2: Improved Ability of Women, Especially Young Women, in Isiolo and Marsabit Counties to Access Public Information and Participate in CountyLevel Governance Processes Under Immediate Outcome 2, IDLO achieved its target of strengthening the ability of women, especially young women, to access public information and participate in county governance processes. The outcome indicator was met, with 71% of young women reporting good or very good capacity to access public information and participate in governance. Key achievements included support to implementation of the Access to Information Act (ATI), awareness and sensitization forums for public officers and communities, development of county reporting tools and guidelines with the Commission on Administrative Justice (CAJ), and the convening of three Annual County Access to Information Conferences. While some output targets were not fully met, the project strengthened both institutional compliance and citizen awareness of information rights. IDLO supported the CAJ to develop a digital Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning system to improve monitoring and reporting on ATI implementation. The MERL system provides a standardized framework for public and private institutions to report on ATI obligations and includes tools for collecting disaggregated data, including gender and agespecific information. The system also enables automated reporting and indicatorbased analysis. Its development was completed in October 2025 and it is currently in use by the CAJ. The project also improved access to information through inclusive and user friendly ATI materials. In partnership with the CAJ and the Kenya Society for the Blind, IDLO developed simplified, Swahili and Braille versions of ATI materials, helping make information rights more accessible to women, youth, persons with visual impairments and other marginalized groups. These materials were disseminated through countyled forums and civil society networks, strengthening public understanding of ATI and supporting more meaningful participation in governance processes, including climate change planning. Draft In addition, IDLO contributed to stronger transparency and accountability systems at county level. The CAJ reported increased and more regular updates on county websites, including Isiolo and Marsabit, while its 2025 research found that 87% of institutions proactively disclosed information, with 76% of that information accessible, mainly through institutional websites. IDLO also supported the development of ATI Bills for Isiolo and Marsabit, which, once enacted, can further institutionalize countylevel ATI obligations and strengthen accountability. Immediate Outcome 3: Improved Capacity of the County Governments of Isiolo and Marsabit to Implement GenderResponsive CountyLevel Climate Change and NRM Actions Under Immediate Outcome 3, IDLO exceeded the outcome target by strengthening county capacity to implement genderresponsive climate change and natural resource management actions. The outcome indicator was overachieved, with 81.3% of county government staff reporting improved capacity. Key achievements included training ELC judges and judicial officers on climate justice and national resource management (NRM), strengthening customary justice actors capacity on conflictsensitive approaches to land and natural resource disputes, and training county attorneys, policymakers, executive officers and implementation committee members on climate change and NRM policy, legal and operational frameworks. Although some output targets related to County Climate Change Units (CCCUs) and implementation committees were not fully achieved, the project strengthened institutional capacity and contributed to more inclusive and genderresponsive climate governance. IDLO supported the County Government of Marsabit to integrate gender responsive actions into the Marsabit County Climate Change Action Plan. The project also supported research on the disproportionate impacts of climate change and NRM on women and girls in Isiolo and Marsabit, which informed the review of the Marsabit Participatory Climate Risk Assessment. These efforts contributed to the inclusion of women and youth in wardlevel climate structures and to the development of a gender mainstreaming toolkit, helping ensure that climate interventions respond to those most affected by water and food insecurity. The project also strengthened coordination mechanisms for climate justice. In collaboration with the Judiciary and National Council on the Administration of Justice (NCAJ), IDLO supported the establishment of Environment and Land Court (ELC) Court User Committees in Isiolo and Marsabit. These committees bring together court actors, county institutions, civil society and communities to improve public participation and coordination on land, environmental and climaterelated matters. They also support the use of AJS and CAM to resolve disputes and restore relationships, contributing to more accessible and context sensitive climate and environmental justice. Finally, IDLO supported the establishment of Gender Committees on Climate Change in Isiolo and Marsabit, integrating 30 women into county climate governance structures. The committees, linked to Ward Planning Committees, provide a mechanism for womens participation in climate finance, project prioritization, implementation and monitoring. This has strengthened public participation and helped ensure that gender equality and inclusion of vulnerable groups are reflected in county climate actions.
